title: Commitment windows and canary scheduling for hosted API model catalog
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Define a repeatable cadence for model catalog commitments and a deterministic canary scheduling system for hosted API model releases. This ticket scopes the operational policy (commitment windows), the canary traffic/time scheduling approach, rollback/automatic-fallback triggers, and the monitoring/eval gating required before promoting a model to full traffic.

Goals:
- Create commitment windows (timeboxed periods) that align PM, Research, and Eng for model selection and freeze (recommended: 2-week soft windows + monthly hard windows).
- Define canary schedules that balance rapid detection with customer stability: progressive traffic ramps (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) and minimum observation windows per step.
- Specify automatic rollback triggers (quality regressions on eval set, latency p99 increase > 20% vs baseline, error rate > 0.5% absolute) and manual-review gates.
- Produce runbooks and automation playbooks to apply canary schedules via the deployment system and Console rollout controls.
- Instrument dashboards and synthetic/eval suites to verify responses and cost impact during canary.

Scope / Non-goals:
- IN SCOPE: Hosted API model catalog releases, Canary scheduling policies, commit cadence recommendation, SLO thresholds, alerting rules, runbooks, brief infra API changes required for scheduled ramps.
- OUT OF SCOPE: Dedicated private deployments rollout playbooks (handled separately), model retraining or evaluation pipeline rewrites.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A written policy describing commitment windows and a calendar template for PM/Research/Eng coordination.
2) Canary schedule YAML schema that the deployments team can consume to drive progressive traffic shifts.
3) Automated gating hooks: evaluation results ingestion, latency/cost checks, and a configured alert set in Console.
4) Runbook with rollback decision tree and owners, plus at least one dry-run simulation documented in logs/PR.
5) Dashboard tiles in Console: canary health (latency, error rate), eval-score delta, token-cost delta, and traffic split.

Metrics to track:
- Time from model selection to full promotion (target < 10 business days).
- Canary detection mean time (target < 60 minutes on synthetic fails).
- Percentage of promotions requiring rollback (target < 5%).
- Median cost delta during canary (target < 10% increase).

Tradeoffs / considerations:
- Short windows accelerate iteration but increase risk of regression slipping into production. We recommend a hybrid approach: 2-week soft windows for discovery and a monthly hard window for production eligibility.
- Traffic ramp aggressiveness should be tied to historical variance on similar model families; default is conservative but policy must allow exceptions with stakeholder signoff.
- Automated rollback thresholds are conservative by default and must be tunable per-model-family.

Next steps / implementation plan:
1) PM writes final policy doc and calendar templates (due 2026-03-17).
2) Eng creates Canary schedule YAML schema + minimal deployment API changes (ENG-1842).
3) Research owners provide model-family-specific baselines and eval sets (dependency ENG-2571).
4) Observability creates dashboard tiles and alert rules (Console work).
5) Run 1 dry-run promotion with synthetic traffic and document outcome, then iterate.
